query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A minor alloying addition of aluminum (approximately 2–3 at.%) to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will improve its oxygen resistance at high temperatures by promoting the in situ formation of a continuous, slow-growing protective Al2O3 scale while largely preserving its room- and high-temperature mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr without any additional reactive element
generation.intervention: Introduce a minor aluminum content (2–3 at.%) during alloy processing to modify the bulk composition
generation.conditions: Exposure in air at temperatures between 800 °C and 1000 °C, with exposure times on the order of 5 hours, under strain rates in the range of 10^(-4) to 10^(-2) s^(-1) (or under static conditions for oxidation testing)
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a thin, adherent Al2O3 layer that acts as a diffusion barrier to oxygen
generation.mechanism: The small aluminum addition will segregate to the surface during high-temperature exposure and oxidize preferentially to form a continuous alumina scale. This oxide layer has low oxygen diffusivity, thereby slowing further oxidation (pesting) and protecting the underlying alloy without significantly compromising the alloy’s mechanical performance at room or high temperatures.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, the Al-doped alloy will show markedly improved oxygen resistance (reduced oxidation penetration and scale spallation) after 5-hour air exposure at ~800 °C to 1000 °C, with yield strength and tensile ductility maintained within the useful range for high-temperature applications.
generation.baseline: Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility and yield strengths of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C with inadequate oxygen resistance during similar conditions
generation.boundary: The intervention is applicable within the temperature range of 800–1000 °C in air with exposure times around 5 hours; mechanical performance is evaluated at room temperature and high temperature under strain rates of 10^(-4) to 10^(-2) s^(-1)
generation.uncertainty: The precise effects of the minor aluminum addition on phase stability and microstructural evolution of the equiatomic matrix are not fully known. It is uncertain if 2–3 at.% Al will be optimal for forming a protective alumina scale without adversely affecting mechanical properties.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr and one set doped with 2–3 at.% Al. Subject both sets to air exposure at 800 °C for 5 hours. Monitor the formation and adherence of the oxide scales via surface microscopy and cross-sectional analysis. Evaluate mechanical properties (tensile ductility at room temperature and yield strength at 1000 °C) for both sample sets.
measurements: Oxide scale thickness, continuity, and adherence using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS)
Oxygen uptake or mass gain measurements during oxidation
Mechanical testing results for tensile ductility and high-temperature yield strength
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al-doped samples do not exhibit a significant reduction in oxidation (i.e., similar oxide scale disruption, mass gain, or oxygen penetration) or if the addition of Al leads to a statistically significant degradation of the targeted mechanical properties relative to the untreated alloy, then the hypothesis is falsified.
